title: Local geometry and differential rank of smooth trait schemes
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, fraction field $E$ and residue field $k$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:Z\to T$ be a smooth finite-type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $Z_E,Z_k$ denote its fibres [def-pc-base-change]. Then $Z$ is Noetherian and regular [def-weil-regular-scheme], and its local rings are integrally closed domains. The open $Z_E\subset Z$ is quasi-compact and schematically dense: restriction $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_{Z_E}$ is injective. The special fibre is reduced, has finitely many irreducible components, and these components are pairwise disjoint open-and-closed subsets of $Z_k$. For the generic point $\zeta$ of each nonempty special-fibre component, $\mathcal O_{Z,\zeta}$ is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer the image of $\pi$. If $Z_E$ is nonempty and pure of dimension $d\geq0$, then $\Omega^1_{Z/R}$ is locally free of constant rank $d$ and $\Omega^d_{Z/R}=\bigwedge^d\Omega^1_{Z/R}$ is invertible [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power, def-sc-invertible-module]. Here pure dimension $d$ means that all irreducible components of the finite-type $E$-scheme $Z_E$ have dimension $d$.

proof.text: Every ideal of $R$ is principal, hence finitely generated, so $R$ is Noetherian. By [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one] its dimension is one; its maximal ideal $(\pi)$ therefore makes it regular local by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], $R$ is a regular ring. A nonzero prime properly below $(\pi)$ would give a prime chain of length two, so the primes of $R$ are $(0)$ and $(\pi)$. Every nonzero denominator is a unit times a power of $\pi$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], whence $R[1/\pi]=E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}E=D(\pi)\subset T$. An open of $T$ containing its closed point is all of $T$ (a basic open containing that point is defined by a unit); thus every nonempty affine open of $T$ is either $T$ or $\operatorname{Spec}E$. Their coordinate rings are regular, the field case following immediately from the dimension-zero definition.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr; Tag 0AFS, lemma-localization-of-regular-local-is-regular; schemes.tex Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine

proof.text: The affine scheme $T$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and locally Noetherian by its single Noetherian affine chart [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $f$ to obtain that $Z$ is Noetherian. The affine-local description in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] gives a covering by $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ mapping to nonempty affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $T$, with $A\to B$ smooth. Step 1 makes $A$ regular, so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] makes $B$ regular. These charts prove that $Z$ is regular. By [rem-pc-regular-normal](1), every local ring of $Z$ is an integrally closed domain.

source.place: Tag 07NF, lemma-regular-goes-up; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; properties.tex Tags 02IT and 0569

proof.text: By [lem-pc-smooth-flat], $f$ is flat. Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] identify $Z_E$ with the open $f^{-1}D(\pi)$; on each smooth affine chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of Step 2 it is $D(\pi_B)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-pullback]. If the chart maps into $\operatorname{Spec}E$, then $\pi_B$ is a unit. Otherwise its base ring is $R$, and $B$ is flat over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]. Apply [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] to multiplication by the nonzero $\pi$ on $R$: after tensoring with $B$ it is multiplication by $\pi_B$, hence this multiplication is injective. With $n=1$, [lem-trf-affine-schematic-density-criterion] now gives the sheaf injection on $W$. These injections on an open covering give $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_{Z_E}$ injective. Moreover [lem-pc-principal-open-dense-of-nonzerodivisor] on the same charts gives topological density of $Z_E$ in $Z$.

source.place: Tag 01VF, lemma-smooth-flat; algebra.tex Tag 0565, lemma-when-injective-covering; Tag 01RE, lemma-characterize-scheme-theoretically-dense; divisors.tex Tag 07ZU, lemma-complement-effective-Cartier-divisor

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] to the open $Z_E\subset Z$ of Step 3 and the Noetherian scheme of Step 2. It makes $Z_E$ Noetherian and in particular quasi-compact. This also covers the empty open.

By [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion], both residue-field fibres of $f$ are smooth over their fields. They are of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (fields are Noetherian and their one-point spectra are quasi-compact). By [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal], $Z_k$ is reduced and normal. Apply [rem-pc-regular-normal](2), whose hypothesis is Noetherianity and normality, to $Z_k$. It gives finitely many pairwise disjoint open-and-closed irreducible components, each with its open subscheme structure normal and integral. For $Z_k=\varnothing$ the component assertions are vacuous.

source.place: Tag 056T, lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal; morphisms.tex Tags 01T4 and 01T6; properties.tex Tag 033M, lemma-normal-Noetherian

proof.text: Let $C$ be one of the nonempty components from Step 5 and $\zeta$ its generic point, which exists by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Since $C$ is integral and open in $Z_k$, [lem-sc-rational-functions-generic-stalks] makes $\mathcal O_{Z_k,\zeta}=\mathcal O_{C,\zeta}$ a field. Put $B=\mathcal O_{Z,\zeta}$. By [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient], $B/\pi B\cong\mathcal O_{Z_k,\zeta}$, so $\pi B$ is the maximal ideal of the local ring $B$. The base stalk at the closed point is $R_{(\pi)}=R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], since elements outside $(\pi)$ are units. Flatness of $f$ means that $B$ is flat over this $R$ [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Tensoring the injection $R\xrightarrow{\pi}R$ with $B$ using [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] makes multiplication by $\pi$ injective on $B$. Since $B$ is a nonzero local domain by Step 2, its element $\pi$ is nonzero. The ring $B$ is Noetherian by regularity. Apply [lem-sc-principal-ideal-dvr]: $B$ is a DVR, and $\pi B=\mathfrak m_B$ says exactly that the image of $\pi$ is its uniformizer.

source.place: Tags 01IS, lemma-scheme-sober, and 0HA1, lemma-local-ring-fibre; morphisms.tex Tag 01RV; algebra.tex Tag 00PD (4)

proof.text: Assume now $Z_E\ne\varnothing$ and that all its irreducible components have dimension $d$. By [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension], applied over $E$ with $O=Z_E$, its local topological dimension at every point is $d$. Set $\mathcal M=\Omega^1_{Z/R}$. It is finite locally free by [lem-ag-smooth-relative-differentials-finite-locally-free]. Fix any $z\in Z$ and a nonempty trivializing neighbourhood $W$ on which $\mathcal M$ has some finite rank $r$. Density from Step 3 gives $y\in W\cap Z_E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension] to $f$ at $y$: it gives an affine neighbourhood on which the differential module is free of rank $\dim_y Z_E=d$. By [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], this is a trivialization of the same sheaf $\mathcal M$. Taking its stalk at $y$ and tensoring with $\kappa(y)$, the two trivializations give an isomorphism $\kappa(y)^r\cong\kappa(y)^d$, hence $r=d$. Thus all these neighbourhoods have rank $d$, which proves constant rank on all of $Z$, including points of the special fibre.

Apply [lem-sc-exterior-sheaf-top-invertible] to $\mathcal M$ of constant rank $d$ from Step 7. Its top exterior power $\Omega^d_{Z/R}=\bigwedge^d\mathcal M$ is locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_Z$. It is quasi-coherent directly by [pqf-def-coherent]: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ refining such a trivialization it is the sheaf associated with the module $A$. Thus it is invertible in [def-sc-invertible-module]. For $d=0$, [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power] identifies it with $\mathcal O_Z$, so this case is included.

Eight steps, no new nodes, statement unchanged. The three stmt_deps added (locnoeth, normal-ring, finite-locally-free-module) are the notions the statement already uses. Step-by-step check: S1: R is a PID, so Noetherian, of dim 1 (00PD), regular local, regular ring by 0AFS; its primes are (0) and (π), R[1/π]=E, Spec E=D(π) by 01I3. S2: Z is Noetherian by 01T6; smooth charts over the regular rings R and E are regular by 07NF; 0569 gives normal local domains. S3: Z_E=f^{-1}D(π)=D(π_B) on charts; B is R-flat, so the Mathlib flat-tensor leaf makes π_B a nonzerodivisor, and the 0565 criterion with n=1 gives O→j_*O injective; 07ZU gives density. S4: Z_E is quasi-compact by 01OW. S5: smooth fibres (smooth criterion), finite type and Noetherian; 056T with K=k gives reduced normal; rem-pc-regular-normal(2) gives disjoint clopen integral components. S6: the generic stalk of C is a field (01RV); 0HA1 with O_{T,s}=R (01HV) gives B/πB a field; flatness makes π a nonzerodivisor; lem-sc-principal-ideal-dvr gives a DVR with m=(π), which is the uniformizer of def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring. S7: dim_y Z_E=d everywhere (0A21; the two dim_x definitions coincide); density puts a point of Z_E in every trivialising neighbourhood, and comparing with the rank-d chart from 02G1 at that point via ⊗κ(y) gives constant rank d. S8: the top exterior power is locally O and quasi-coherent, so invertible; d=0 is covered. Small cases checked: Spec R, Spec E, empty Z, A^n_R, nonperfect residue field. Batch-5: lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection (a Mathlib leaf), lem-trf-affine-schematic-density-criterion (0565, closure is algebra only) and lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal (056T, closure is generic geometry; its only sec-poincare-duality node is a finite-type base-change lemma) lie outside both assumptions and are accepted. No duplicate found (rg -L over dag/nodes). I accept the generic tool_uses in split_report.
